about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Bernardino, California
about.longDescription: San Bernardino sits where I-215 and SR-210 meet, and much of daily life here moves along those two highways plus surface streets like E Highland Avenue and W Baseline Street. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, the city recorded 1,380 injury collisions. Those crashes left 2,068 people hurt, and 32 lives were lost. The counts are public record, and they describe a city of 216,108 residents where getting injured in traffic is not unusual. Reported collisions tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., as the workweek winds down and commuters head home. If you were hurt in one of those crashes, or on a wet floor in a store, or by a dog in your own neighborhood, you likely have questions about medical bills, missed paychecks, and what comes next. We handle personal injury claims in San Bernardino County. Our team works on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most injured people two years to file a claim, but a claim against a city or county agency can carry a deadline as short as six months, so talking with someone early matters. Contact us to discuss your case.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your San Bernardino Claim

items.title: Two Years to Act, Sometimes Far Less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a public sidewalk, the window can shrink to six months, so timing is not something to leave for later.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Does Not End Your Case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame for a crash on W Baseline Street, your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than wiped out.

items.title: Pain and Suffering Is Not Capped
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, lost enjoyment of life, and emotional distress. Your claim can reflect the full effect an injury has had on you.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. You do not pay hourly fees or a retainer, and we are paid only if your case results in a recovery.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in San Bernardino?
items.answer: Public collision records show that SR-210, I-215, E Highland Avenue, and W Baseline Street carry the highest counts of reported crashes in the city. These are also among the busiest routes for daily traffic. Records also show reported crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of the injury. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a public bus or a hazard on city property, you may have only six months to file a formal claim. We can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are a personal injury practice handling cases in San Bernardino County. We do not provide legal advice through this service; we handle your case directly. When you contact us, you work with us from the start.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system. Being partly responsible reduces your recovery by your share of fault, but it does not bar you from recovering. Even someone found mostly at fault can still recover the remaining portion.

items.question: What will it cost me to talk with an attorney?
items.answer: Contacting us is free, and we work on contingency. That means no hourly charges and no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You can ask questions and understand your options before deciding anything.
